# The anchor gap

*Generated by `make anchors-report`. Do not hand-edit.*

`IndexSpec.reference_level` describes itself as "nominal" and cites nothing.
It sets the scale of every price this project publishes. These are the real
public prices it sits against, and the distance between them.

**The reference levels are not being changed.** They seed the simulator, the
fleet's quotes and the tape's price pin, so moving them would break
comparability with the prints already on chain. That is a separate decision.
What this file does is stop the gap being invisible.

The quality metrics are immune to it either way: the simulator draws notional
first and derives size, so every bp-denominated figure is exactly
scale-invariant — measured, by re-anchoring ACR-INF 667x and watching
`attack_acr_err_bp` not move at all.

| index | reference | market anchor | gap | rows | spread | as of |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ACR-INF` | 0.5 $/1k tokens | 0.0004 | **1250x** | 5/10 | 2.7x | 2026-10-31 |
| `ACR-GPU` | 0.011 $/GPU-sec | 0.001075 | **10x** | 10/10 | 8.4x | 2026-10-31 |
| `ACR-DATA` | 0.002 $/MB | 9e-05 | **22x** | 3/3 | 1.4x | 2026-10-31 |

## Why the gap is not one number

It is a function of the aggregation rule, and the rule swings it several-fold.
For ACR-INF the same catalogue gives roughly 1000x on a prompt-only median,
588x on the 75/25 blend this basket uses, and 335x on a trimmed mean over
every priced model. A gap quoted without its rule is not a measurement, so
each anchor records its `selection` and every row's own source.

## Per index

### ACR-INF — $/1k tokens

ACR-INF estimates the constant-quality price of a MID-class seller at 250ms (acr_estimator/hedonic.py REF_MODEL_CLASS, REF_LATENCY_MS). A median over a whole catalogue is not that: it runs down to $1.7e-08/token on open-weights models, which the hedonic stage would adjust away rather than average in. So the basket is a named mid-tier selection, and the fetch supplies prices for these rows only.

### ACR-GPU — $/GPU-sec

Published on-demand rate cards, plus live prices from Bittensor subnet 51 (Lium). Until 2026-10-29 this basket said no GPU cloud published a clean unauthenticated price JSON; that is no longer true — https://lium.io/api/executors serves every executor with its price, tier and accelerator model, no key. Those rows are now fetched over HTTP; the rate-card rows stay curated, each carrying the URL a human can check, because they are the comparison set a reader expects to see. On-demand only: spot and marketplace bids are a different product with a different risk, and mixing them would make the aggregate a blend of two markets — Lium labels these `tier`, and 36 of 130 executors were spot and excluded. Datacenter accelerators only, which is the same rule `rule.note` has always stated: including Lium's consumer RTX cards would take the basket to 94 rows with a 44x spread and a 49.5x gap, and a basket whose rows span 44x has no single price. That number is disclosed here rather than buried, because excluding rows is exactly the move a reader should be able to check.

### ACR-DATA — $/MB

Metered egress from the three hyperscalers, at first-tier public list price. Cloudflare R2 charges $0.00 for egress and is deliberately EXCLUDED from the aggregate: zero is a different business model rather than a cheaper price, and one zero in a basket of four halves the median. It is recorded here as a market fact a reader should know, not as a row.

| row | price | source |

| AWS data transfer out, first 10TB | 9e-05 | [$0.09/GB, us-east-1, first 10 TB/month](https://aws.amazon.com/ec2/pricing/on-demand/) |
